### Shared helpers

Everything that was copy-pasted in the original lives here once.

```{r}
weekday_levels <- c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday",
                    "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday")

# Hours treated as "closed". NOTE: the original used three different definitions
# in different places; they are kept separate here so results do not change,
# but you may want to settle on one.
hour_labels       <- function(h) sprintf("%02d:00:00", h)
excl_hours_assoc  <- hour_labels(c(20:23, 0:9))   # association figure / open-hours data
excl_hours_logit  <- hour_labels(c(21:23, 0:9))   # combined logit, hours excluded
excl_hours_mixed  <- hour_labels(0:7)             # mixed-effects model

# McFadden pseudo-R2
mcfadden <- function(model, null) 1 - as.numeric(logLik(model)) / as.numeric(logLik(null))

# Incidents / suspensions / suspension rate by any grouping (data is one row per incident)
susp_summary <- function(data, ...) {
  data %>%
    group_by(...) %>%
    summarise(
      n_incidents     = n_distinct(`Incident ID`),
      n_suspensions   = sum(susp_binary, na.rm = TRUE),
      suspension_rate = mean(susp_binary, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Cramér's V from a 2 x k contingency of outcome x predictor (0 if degenerate)
cramers_v <- function(x, y) {
  tab <- table(x, y)
  if (nrow(tab) < 2 || ncol(tab) < 2) return(0)
  chi <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE)$statistic),
                  error = function(e) NA_real_)
  res <- as.numeric(sqrt(chi / (sum(tab) * (min(dim(tab)) - 1))))
  if (is.na(res) || is.nan(res)) 0 else res
}

# Cramér's V + Nagelkerke pseudo-R2 for each single predictor of an outcome
assoc_metrics <- function(data, predictors, outcome_var = "susp_binary") {
  map_df(predictors, function(pred) {
    clean_df <- data %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome_var]]), !is.na(.data[[pred]]))

    v_val <- cramers_v(clean_df[[outcome_var]], clean_df[[pred]])

    fit <- suppressWarnings(
      glm(as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~", pred)),
          data = clean_df, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
    )
    pseudo_r2 <- tryCatch(as.numeric(performance::r2_nagelkerke(fit)),
                          error = function(e) NA_real_)

    data.frame(Predictor = pred,
               Cramers_V = round(v_val, 4),
               Pseudo_R2_Nagelkerke = round(pseudo_r2, 4))
  }) %>%
    arrange(desc(Pseudo_R2_Nagelkerke))
}

# Print model summary, McFadden R2 and LRT against the null model
summarize_logit <- function(model, null) {
  print(summary(model))
  cat("McFadden pseudo-R²:", round(mcfadden(model, null), 4), "\n")
  print(anova(null, model, test = "LRT"))
}

# Drop-one likelihood-ratio tests for a full model (location / weekday / hour)
drop_one_lrt <- function(full,
                         terms = c(Location = "Location_masked",
                                   Weekday  = "PITS_weekday",
                                   Hour     = "hour_label"),
                         suffix = "") {
  for (nm in names(terms)) {
    reduced <- update(full, as.formula(paste(". ~ . -", terms[[nm]])))
    cat("\nDoes removing", nm, "hurt the model", suffix, "?\n")
    print(anova(reduced, full, test = "LRT"))
  }
}

# "p < .001" / "p = .123" labels for table footnotes
p_label <- function(p) if (p < .001) "p < .001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", p)
fmt_p   <- function(x) ifelse(x < .001, "< .001", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", x)))

# Shared gt styling and saving
style_gt <- function(tbl) {
  tbl %>%
    opt_align_table_header("left") %>%
    tab_options(
      column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
      table.border.top.style    = "solid",
      table.border.bottom.style = "solid",
      data_row.padding          = px(4)
    )
}
save_gt <- function(tbl, name) {
  gtsave(tbl, paste0(name, ".docx"))   # Word
  gtsave(tbl, paste0(name, ".png"))
}

# Dunn's post hoc test (tie-corrected, two-sided, Bonferroni), returns a data frame
dunn_bonferroni <- function(x, g) {
  d <- tibble(x = x, g = as.character(g)) %>% filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(g))
  N <- nrow(d)
  d$r <- rank(d$x)
  t_ties <- table(d$x)
  sigma2 <- N * (N + 1) / 12 - sum(t_ties^3 - t_ties) / (12 * (N - 1))
  grp <- d %>% group_by(g) %>% summarise(n = n(), mean_rank = mean(r), .groups = "drop")
  combn(grp$g, 2, simplify = FALSE) %>%
    map_dfr(function(p) {
      a <- grp[grp$g == p[1], ]; b <- grp[grp$g == p[2], ]
      z <- (a$mean_rank - b$mean_rank) / sqrt(sigma2 * (1 / a$n + 1 / b$n))
      tibble(group1 = p[1], group2 = p[2], z = z, p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z)))
    }) %>%
    mutate(p_adj = pmin(1, p.adjust(p, method = "bonferroni"))) %>%
    arrange(p_adj)
}
```

### Recode parsed categories

```{r}
PITS_public <- PITS_public %>%
  mutate(parsed_categories = recode(
    parsed_categories,
    "Children in the Library" = "Unattended Children",
    "Use and preservation of library materials and property" =
      "Damage to library materials and property"
  ))
```

```{r}
table(PITS_public$susp_binary, useNA = "ifany")
```

### Add day of the week, month and season

```{r}
PITS_public$PITS_weekday <- weekdays(PITS_public$Date2)
PITS_public <- PITS_public %>%
  mutate(PITS_weekday = factor(PITS_weekday, levels = weekday_levels))

PITS_public <- PITS_public %>%
  mutate(
    month_num   = as.integer(format(Date2, "%m")),
    month_name  = factor(format(Date2, "%B"), levels = month.name),  # orders Jan–Dec correctly
    season      = case_when(
      month_num %in% c(6, 7, 8)   ~ "Summer",
      month_num %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Fall",
      month_num %in% c(12, 1, 2)  ~ "Winter",
      month_num %in% c(3, 4, 5)   ~ "Spring",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    season = factor(season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall"))
  )


```

## Categories table (all occurrences, multi-selection allowed)

```{r}
# 1. True count and percentage of all category occurrences (no distinct)
cat_counts <- PITS_public %>%
  filter(!is.na(parsed_categories)) %>%
  count(parsed_categories, name = "total_category_instances") %>%
  mutate(pct_of_all_categories = total_category_instances / sum(total_category_instances) * 100)

# 2. Unique incident counts and suspension rates (distinct incident x category)
cat_suspensions <- PITS_public %>%
  filter(!is.na(parsed_categories)) %>%
  distinct(`Incident ID`, parsed_categories, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  group_by(parsed_categories) %>%
  summarise(
    unique_incidents = n(),
    n_suspended      = sum(susp_binary, na.rm = TRUE),
    suspension_rate  = mean(susp_binary, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,   # converted to %
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3. Combine
categories_table <- cat_counts %>%
  left_join(cat_suspensions, by = "parsed_categories") %>%
  arrange(desc(unique_incidents))

print(categories_table)
```

```{r}
categories_gt <- categories_table %>%
  dplyr::select(parsed_categories, total_category_instances,
                pct_of_all_categories, suspension_rate) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_category_instances)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title    = "Infraction Categories and Suspension Rates",
    subtitle = "Public library incidents, 2023–2025"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    parsed_categories        = "Infraction category",
    total_category_instances = "Occurrences",
    pct_of_all_categories    = "% of All Occurrences",

  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = total_category_instances, decimals = 0, use_seps = TRUE) %>%

  cols_width(parsed_categories ~ px(320), everything() ~ px(120)) %>%
```

## Pre-compute suspension ratio data (suspensions per incident + avg length)

```{r}
# One row per unique suspended incident — prevents duration double-counting
PITS_susp_deduped <- PITS_public %>%
  distinct(`Incident ID`, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(susp_binary == 1,
         !is.na(`Incident ID`),
         !is.na(Suspension_length)) %>%
  dplyr::select(`Incident ID`, Location_masked, Date2, Suspension_length)

# Suspensions per location per day
PITS_susp_counts <- PITS_susp_deduped %>%
  group_by(Location_masked, date = as.Date(Date2)) %>%
  summarise(
    suspension_count   = n(),
    avg_susp_length    = mean(Suspension_length),
    median_susp_length = median(Suspension_length),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# again severity will come into play later
susp_ratio_data <- PITS_incident_counts %>%
  left_join(PITS_susp_counts, by = c("Location_masked", "date")) %>%
  mutate(
    suspension_count   = replace_na(suspension_count,   0),
    avg_susp_length    = replace_na(avg_susp_length,    0),
    median_susp_length = replace_na(median_susp_length, 0),
    susp_ratio         = ifelse(incident_count > 0, suspension_count / incident_count, 0)
  )
```

### One-sample proportion test: is the suspension rate \> 50%?

```{r}
# H0: true suspension rate = 0.50;  H1: true suspension rate > 0.50
binom_test <- binom.test(
  x = suspension_summary$total_suspensions,
  n = suspension_summary$total_incidents,
  p = 0.50,
  alternative = "greater"
)
binom_test
```

## SECTION 2: Predictors — Cramér's V, pseudo-R², Kruskal-Wallis, Dunn

### Establish the deduplicated dataset (one row per incident, most severe infraction wins)

```{r}
severity_hierarchy <- c(
  "Dangerous, Threatening, or Illegal Conduct",
  "Disruptive Personal Behavior",
  "Damage to library materials and property",
  "Incident Impact Level - Staff Traumatic Stress",
  "Other",
  "Unattended Children",
  "No Infractions Set",
  "Medical 911"
)

PITS_deduplicated <- PITS_public %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(parsed_categories),
    parsed_categories %in% severity_hierarchy
  ) %>%
  mutate(parsed_categories = factor(parsed_categories,
                                    levels = severity_hierarchy,
                                    ordered = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(`Incident ID`, parsed_categories) %>%
  distinct(`Incident ID`, .keep_all = TRUE)   # each incident counts exactly once

PITS_deduplicated <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
  mutate(susp_binary = replace_na(susp_binary, 0))
# Grouped "Minor Infractions" category
# NOTE: "Medical" below does not match "Medical 911" in severity_hierarchy, so
# Medical 911 stays its own category. Left as-is so results do not change.
PITS_deduplicated <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
  mutate(
    parsed_categories1 = as.character(parsed_categories),
    parsed_categories1 = case_when(
      parsed_categories1 %in% c(
        "Incident Impact Level - Staff Traumatic Stress",
        "No Infractions Set",
        "Medical",
        "Other",
        "Unattended Children"
      ) ~ "Minor Infractions",
      TRUE ~ parsed_categories
    )
  )
```

Publishable version of the table

```{r}
predictor_labels <- c(
  parsed_categories1 = "Infraction Category",
  Location_masked    = "Branch Location",
  hour_label         = "Hour of day",
  PITS_weekday       = "Day of week",
  season             = "Season",
  month_name         = "Month"
)

plot_df <- metrics_table_hr %>%
  mutate(Predictor = fct_reorder(recode(Predictor, !!!predictor_labels),
                                 Pseudo_R2_Nagelkerke)) %>%        # highest at top
  pivot_longer(c(Cramers_V, Pseudo_R2_Nagelkerke),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric,
                         levels = c("Pseudo_R2_Nagelkerke", "Cramers_V"),
                         labels = c("Nagelkerke pseudo-R\u00b2", "Cram\u00e9r's V")))

assoc_plot <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = value, y = Predictor)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, fill = "#4A6A8A") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", value)), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.4, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Association Between Each Predictor and Suspension",
    subtitle = "Single-predictor comparisons, incidents excluding Sundays and 20:00\u201309:00",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = "Note: Each predictor was assessed on its own. Pseudo-R\u00b2 is from a logistic regression of suspension on that predictor."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position   = "plot",
    plot.title            = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle         = element_text(colour = "grey35", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption          = element_text(colour = "grey35", hjust = 0, size = 9, margin = margin(t = 10)),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    strip.text            = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.x    = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor      = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y    = element_line(colour = "grey88", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.text.y           = element_text(colour = "grey10", size = 11),
    axis.text.x           = element_text(colour = "grey35"),
    panel.spacing         = unit(1.5, "lines"),
    plot.margin           = margin(12, 16, 10, 12)
  )

assoc_plot
ggsave("cramer_nagelkerke_predictor_association.png", assoc_plot,
       width = 9, height = 4.2, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
# For a journal, also save as vector: ggsave("predictor_association.pdf", assoc_plot, width = 9, height = 4.2)
```

### Test collinearity

```{r}
collinearity_df <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
  filter(!is.na(susp_binary))

logit_collinearity <- glm(
  susp_binary ~ parsed_categories1 + Location_masked + hour_label + PITS_weekday + month_name,
  data   = collinearity_df,
  family = binomial
)

check_collinearity(logit_collinearity)
```
Variance inflation factors were low for all predictors (adjusted VIF ≤ 1.20), indicating no problematic multicollinearity.

```{r}
# McNemar test: suspension vs. guard called (contingency table of the two binary variables)
mcnemar_df <- PITS_public %>%
  distinct(`Incident ID`, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    guard_called = ifelse(`Support:Called Guard?` == "Yes", 1L, 0L),

  guard_called = mcnemar_df$guard_called
```

## SECTION 2 (Main): Logistic regression — does reporting predict suspension better than incident characteristics do?

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# One modeling frame, reused for every model below
pits_model_df <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
  filter(!is.na(susp_binary),
         !is.na(parsed_categories1),
         !is.na(hour_label),
         !is.na(Location_masked),
         !is.na(PITS_weekday)) %>%
  mutate(
    infraction_cat = as.factor(parsed_categories1),
    location       = as.factor(Location_masked),
    weekday        = as.factor(PITS_weekday),
    hour           = as.factor(hour_label)
  )

# Null model (intercept only — "reporting alone")
logit_null <- glm(susp_binary ~ 1, data = pits_model_df, family = binomial)

# Full model with incident characteristics
logit_full <- glm(susp_binary ~ infraction_cat + hour + weekday + location,
                  data = pits_model_df, family = binomial)

# McFadden R2 (low value supports the argument that observable characteristics
# don't explain suspension well) + LRT against the null
summarize_logit(logit_full, logit_null)

logit_tidy <- tidy(logit_full, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  arrange(p.value)
print(logit_tidy)
```

Different logit model: location + hour only

```{r}
logit_loc_hour <- glm(susp_binary ~ location + hour,
                      data = pits_model_df, family = binomial)
summarize_logit(logit_loc_hour, logit_null)
```

## SECTION 3: Chi-square — suspensions not proportional to infraction type

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

infraction_susp_table <- table(
  infraction = PITS_deduplicated$parsed_categories1,
  suspended  = PITS_deduplicated$susp_binary
)
print(infraction_susp_table)

chi_infraction <- chisq.test(infraction_susp_table)
print(chi_infraction)

# Table data: incidents, number suspended, and % suspended per category
infraction_susp_df <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
  filter(!is.na(parsed_categories1)) %>%
  group_by(parsed_categories1) %>%
  summarise(
    total         = n(),
    n_suspended   = sum(susp_binary == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_suspended = n_suspended / total * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_suspended), desc(pct_suspended))

# Footnote text: χ²(df) = value, p < .001
chi_note <- sprintf("\u03c7\u00b2(%d) = %.2f, %s",
                    chi_infraction$parameter, chi_infraction$statistic,
                    p_label(chi_infraction$p.value))

infraction_gt <- infraction_susp_df %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title    = "Infraction Categories and Suspension Rates",
    subtitle = "Public library incidents, 2023\u20132025"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    parsed_categories1 = "Infraction category",
    total              = "Number of Incidents",
    n_suspended        = "Number Suspended",
    pct_suspended      = "Suspension Rate (%)"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(total, n_suspended), decimals = 0, use_seps = TRUE) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = pct_suspended, decimals = 1) %>%
  cols_align("left",  columns = parsed_categories1) %>%
  cols_align("right", columns = -parsed_categories1) %>%
  cols_width(parsed_categories1 ~ px(320), everything() ~ px(120)) %>%
  tab_source_note(paste0("Note: Pearson's chi-square test of association between infraction category and suspension, ",
                         chi_note, ". Categories are sorted by number of suspensions.")) %>%
  style_gt()

infraction_gt
save_gt(infraction_gt, "infraction_table")
```

## SECTION 4: Kruskal-Wallis — suspension length not calibrated to infraction

Tests whether suspension length varies by infraction category — if it doesn't, lengths aren't being calibrated to severity either.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Suspended incidents only (already one row per incident), with a valid length
susp_length_df <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
  filter(susp_binary == 1,
         !is.na(Suspension_length),
         !is.na(parsed_categories1))

# Descriptives by infraction category
length_by_infraction <- susp_length_df %>%
  group_by(parsed_categories1) %>%
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    min_days    = min(Suspension_length),
    median_days = median(Suspension_length),
    mean_days   = mean(Suspension_length),
    max_days    = max(Suspension_length),
    sd_days     = sd(Suspension_length),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(median_days))

print(length_by_infraction)

# Kruskal-Wallis
kw_length <- kruskal.test(Suspension_length ~ as.factor(parsed_categories1),
                          data = susp_length_df)
print(kw_length)

# Dunn post hoc (Bonferroni)
dunn_df <- dunn_bonferroni(susp_length_df$Suspension_length,
                           susp_length_df$parsed_categories1)
print(dunn_df)

# Optional: effect size and Holm-adjusted pairs
# susp_length_df %>% kruskal_effsize(Suspension_length ~ parsed_categories1)
# susp_length_df %>% dunn_test(Suspension_length ~ parsed_categories1, p.adjust.method = "holm")
```

```{r}
suspensions_gt <- length_by_infraction %>%
  dplyr::select(parsed_categories1, n, median_days, mean_days,
                sd_days, min_days, max_days) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title    = "Infraction Categories and Suspension Lengths",

  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    parsed_categories1 = "Infraction category",
    n                  = "Number of Suspensions",
    median_days        = "Median (days)",
    mean_days          = "Mean (days)",

    min_days           = "Min (days)",
    max_days           = "Max (days)"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(n, min_days, max_days), decimals = 0, use_seps = TRUE) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(median_days, mean_days, sd_days), decimals = 1) %>%
  sub_missing(columns = sd_days, missing_text = "—") %>%
  cols_align("left",  columns = parsed_categories1) %>%
  cols_align("right", columns = -parsed_categories1) %>%
  cols_width(parsed_categories1 ~ px(320), everything() ~ px(110)) %>%
  tab_source_note("Note: Categories are sorted by number of suspensions.") %>%
  style_gt()

suspensions_gt
save_gt(suspensions_gt, "suspensions_length_table")
```

```{r}
kw_note <- sprintf("Kruskal-Wallis test: H(%d) = %.2f, %s",
                   kw_length$parameter, kw_length$statistic, p_label(kw_length$p.value))

dunn_gt <- dunn_df %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title    = "Pairwise Comparisons of Suspension Length by Infraction Category",
             subtitle = "Dunn post hoc tests, Bonferroni-adjusted") %>%
  cols_label(group1 = "Category 1", group2 = "Category 2", z = "Z",
             p = "p (unadjusted)", p_adj = "p (adjusted)") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = z, decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt(columns = c(p, p_adj), fns = fmt_p) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"), locations = cells_body(rows = p_adj < .05)) %>%
  cols_align("left", columns = c(group1, group2)) %>%
  cols_align("right", columns = -c(group1, group2)) %>%
  cols_width(c(group1, group2) ~ px(260), everything() ~ px(110)) %>%
  tab_source_note(paste0("Note: ", kw_note, ". Pairs in bold are significant after Bonferroni adjustment (adjusted p < .05).")) %>%
  style_gt()

dunn_gt
```

### Suspension length by location

Not so significant once the Dunn p-values are adjusted.

```{r}
susp_length_loc <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
  filter(susp_binary == 1,
         !is.na(Suspension_length),
         !is.na(Location_masked))

susp_length_by_loc <- susp_length_loc %>%
  group_by(Location_masked) %>%
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    median_days = median(Suspension_length),
    mean_days   = mean(Suspension_length),
    sd_days     = sd(Suspension_length),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Location_masked)

print(susp_length_by_loc)

kw_location <- kruskal.test(Suspension_length ~ Location_masked, data = susp_length_loc)
print(kw_location)

dunn_location_df <- dunn_bonferroni(susp_length_loc$Suspension_length,
                                    susp_length_loc$Location_masked)
print(dunn_location_df)
```

## SECTION 6: Chi-square — suspension rates vary by location (inconsistent application)

### Location

Chi-square is significant for location.

```{r}
location_susp_table <- table(
  location  = PITS_deduplicated$Location_masked,
  suspended = PITS_deduplicated$susp_binary
)
print(location_susp_table)

# Is suspension likelihood associated with location?
chi_location <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(location_susp_table))
print(chi_location)

# Logistic regression: location as predictor of suspension
logit_location <- glm(susp_binary ~ Location_masked,
                      data = PITS_deduplicated, family = binomial)
summary(logit_location)
tidy(logit_location, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)

# Branch-level rates, standardized residuals, and share of the chi-square statistic
branch_resid <- tibble(
  location  = rownames(location_susp_table),
  n         = rowSums(location_susp_table),
  suspended = location_susp_table[, "1"],
  rate      = round(100 * suspended / n, 1),
  std_resid = round(chi_location$stdres[, "1"], 2),
  pct_chisq = round(100 * rowSums((location_susp_table - chi_location$expected)^2 / chi_location$expected) /
                      sum((location_susp_table - chi_location$expected)^2 / chi_location$expected), 1)
) %>% arrange(desc(pct_chisq))

branch_resid
branch_resid %>% arrange(desc(std_resid))   # which branches suspend more/less than expected?
```

### Hour

The chi-square for hour_label is significant.

```{r}
hour_table <- table(
  hour      = PITS_deduplicated$hour_label,
  suspended = PITS_deduplicated$susp_binary
)
print(hour_table)

chi_hour <- chisq.test(hour_table)
print(chi_hour)

logit_hour <- glm(susp_binary ~ hour_label, data = PITS_deduplicated, family = binomial)
summary(logit_hour)
```

Cramér's V for location, hour, weekday, season and month is in `metrics_table` above.

```{r}
dow_hour_full <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
```

## SECTION 8: MyPC usage vs incidents by weekday

```{r}
# Summarise MyPC usage by day of week (unique logins, Sundays excluded)
mypc_dow <- MyPC_public %>%
  distinct(new_login_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(MyPC_weekday), MyPC_weekday != "Sunday") %>%
  group_by(MyPC_weekday) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sessions     = n(),
    n_unique_users = n_distinct(new_login_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(mypc_dow)

# Join MyPC usage with incident counts by weekday
dow_combined <- dow_summary %>%
  left_join(mypc_dow, by = c("PITS_weekday" = "MyPC_weekday")) %>%
  mutate(
    incidents_per_100_sessions   = (n_incidents / n_sessions) * 100,
    suspensions_per_100_sessions = (n_suspensions / n_sessions) * 100
  )

print(dow_combined)
```

Do busier days produce more incidents / suspensions? Does higher usage predict a higher suspension *rate*? (The p-value for the rate is too high to say that PC use affects suspension rate.)

```{r}
#| warning: false

cor_sessions <- map(
  c(incidents = "n_incidents", suspensions = "n_suspensions", suspension_rate = "suspension_rate"),
  ~ cor.test(dow_combined$n_sessions, dow_combined[[.x]], method = "spearman")
)

iwalk(cor_sessions, function(res, nm) {
  cat("\nSpearman correlation — sessions vs.", nm, "by weekday:\n")
  print(res)
})
```

## Combined logistic regression — compare the contribution of each predictor

Put location, weekday, and hour into the same model and see which contributes the most explanatory power when the others are controlled for.

```{r}
logit_combined <- glm(
  susp_binary ~ Location_masked + PITS_weekday + hour_label,
  data   = pits_model_df,
  family = binomial
)
summary(logit_combined)

# Drop each block and compare fit via likelihood ratio test (larger stat = term matters more)
drop_one_lrt(logit_combined)
```

```{r}
         !is.na(PITS_weekday), !is.na(hour_label),

  mutate(hour_label = droplevels(hour_label))   # drop the now-unused factor levels

logit_combined_exc <- glm(
  susp_binary ~ Location_masked + PITS_weekday + hour_label,

)
summary(logit_combined_exc)

drop_one_lrt(logit_combined_exc, suffix = "(excluded)")
```

## SECTION 9: Month / Season — do summer months lead to more suspensions?

```{r}
month_summary <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
  filter(!is.na(month_name)) %>%
  susp_summary(month_name)

print(month_summary)

# Month as predictor
logit_month <- glm(
  susp_binary ~ month_name,
  data   = PITS_deduplicated %>% filter(!is.na(month_name)),
  family = binomial
)
cat("\nLogistic regression — month as predictor of suspension:\n")
tidy(logit_month, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>% print()

# Does month matter once location/weekday/hour are controlled for?
logit_no_month <- glm(
  susp_binary ~ Location_masked + PITS_weekday + hour_label,
  data = PITS_deduplicated, family = binomial
)
logit_with_month <- glm(
  susp_binary ~ Location_masked + PITS_weekday + hour_label + month_name,
  data = PITS_deduplicated, family = binomial
)

cat("\nDoes adding Month improve the model (controlling for location/weekday/hour)?\n")
anova(logit_no_month, logit_with_month, test = "LRT")

# Pseudo-R² for month alone, for comparison with the other predictors
logit_null_month  <- glm(susp_binary ~ 1,          data = PITS_deduplicated, family = binomial)
logit_month_alone <- glm(susp_binary ~ month_name, data = PITS_deduplicated, family = binomial)
cat("Pseudo-R² — Month alone:", round(mcfadden(logit_month_alone, logit_null_month), 4), "\n")
```

Month does nothing for this model.

## SECTION 10: Mixed-effects model with season added

Do not use since seasons don't do much.

```{r}
mixed_df <- PITS_deduplicated %>%
  filter(!is.na(susp_binary), !is.na(Location_masked),
         !is.na(PITS_weekday), !is.na(hour_label), !is.na(season)) %>%
  filter(PITS_weekday != "Sunday",
         !hour_label %in% excl_hours_mixed)

# Mixed model: weekday + hour + season as fixed effects, branch as random
mixed_model_season <- glmer(
  susp_binary ~ PITS_weekday + hour_label + season + (1 | Location_masked),
  data    = mixed_df,
  family  = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)
summary(mixed_model_season)

# ICC — how much variance is due to branch, controlling for weekday/hour/season
icc_season <- icc(mixed_model_season)
icc_season

# Compare to the original model (weekday + hour only, no season), same data
mixed_model_original <- glmer(
  susp_binary ~ PITS_weekday + hour_label + (1 | Location_masked),
  data   = mixed_df,
  family = binomial
)
icc_original <- icc(mixed_model_original)

cat("\nICC comparison:\n")
cat("Without season — Adjusted ICC:", round(icc_original$ICC_adjusted, 4),
    "| Unadjusted ICC:", round(icc_original$ICC_unadjusted, 4), "\n")
cat("With season    — Adjusted ICC:", round(icc_season$ICC_adjusted, 4),
    "| Unadjusted ICC:", round(icc_season$ICC_unadjusted, 4), "\n")

# Likelihood ratio test — does adding season improve the mixed model?
cat("\nDoes adding season improve the mixed model?\n")
anova(mixed_model_original, mixed_model_season, test = "LRT")
```

```{r}
# Branch-level random effects (season controlled), ranked
ranef_branch_season <- ranef(mixed_model_season)$Location_masked
ranef_branch_season$Location_masked <- rownames(ranef_branch_season)
names(ranef_branch_season)[1] <- "random_effect"

ranef_branch_season <- ranef_branch_season %>%
  arrange(desc(random_effect))

ranef_branch_season
```
